Subject: Renewal kickoff: StratusAI milestone runbook & QBR scheduling

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our plan to start the renewal/expansion cadence, I’m kicking off a short-run runbook to align stakeholders, confirm the capacity uplift, and lock a QBR slot to finalize commercial terms. High level plan attached (Stratus_Renewal_Runbook_v1.pdf) and a live MAP spreadsheet (MAP_StratusAI_Q3.xlsx) with owners.

Proposed 30–45 minute QBR windows (please pick one):
- Tue Sep 17, 10:00–10:45 PT — prefer if Ben can join
- Wed Sep 18, 14:00–14:45 PT — backup for execs
- Thu Sep 19, 08:30–09:00 PT — quick ops-focused sync

Immediate asks / next steps for this week:
1) Alicia/Ben: confirm preferred QBR slot and list of attendees (exec + procurement + infra).
2) Marissa: can you prepare a 5-min capacity run-rate and expected token throughput for proposed uplift (+30%)?
3) Kimberly: legal/procurement touchpoint — any redlines we should anticipate?
4) Dylan: ops runbook owner — I’ve assigned you to lead the migration checklist and test plan in the MAP.

Goal for the QBR: align on renewed term length (we recommended 12 months with staircase commit), finalize capacity uplift and milestone-based credits, and set sign-off timeline (DocuSign link expected within 5 business days post-QBR).

Attachments: Stratus_Renewal_Runbook_v1.pdf, MAP_StratusAI_Q3.xlsx (Google Drive link below).

Thanks — available after 1pm PT today for a quick pre-call if helpful.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez

- We are targeting a +40% throughput uplift vs current commit to support a new feature launch in Q4. Is the +30% Marissa mentioned a conservative starting point?

Alicia — great, thanks for confirming Wed Sep 18 at 14:00 PT. I’ll block that on our end.

Quick legal/procurement notes so we start with the right intake:
- If StratusAI is moving to a 40% uplift, we’ll need a clearer definition of burst vs committed throughput in the MAP (Marissa — can you add a short table?).
- Standard redlines we anticipate: data residency language if new logs are retained beyond 90 days; indemnity carveouts for third-party hosted models; and a request to shorten the SLA response window for severity-1 incidents. I’ll surface examples in the drive folder (legal_samples/).
- Procurement will likely ask for billing alignment to monthly-in-arrears on the larger uplift; if you have preferred billing cadence let us know (Alicia/Ben).

Sergio — can you confirm who will own the DocuSign flow? We prefer to generate the initial redline track after QBR so the procurement loop is simpler.

Kimberly Park
